definitions.explanation: Both feet or both legs taken together, in contrast to {片足|かたあし} (one foot/leg). Used in everyday descriptions of posture, movement, sports, and medical contexts.

examples.japanese: {両足|りょうあし}でジャンプする。
{両足|りょうあし}を{揃|そろ}えて{座|すわ}ってください。
examples.english: Please sit with your feet together.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}{立|た}ちっぱなしだったので、{両足|りょうあし}がパンパンに{張|は}っている。
examples.english: Because I was standing for a long time, both my legs are tight and swollen.

notes:
Compound of {両|りょう} (both) + {足|あし} (foot/leg). The prefix {両|りょう} attaches to paired body parts to mean "both —".

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {両足|りょうあし}を{揃|そろ}える: to put one's feet together
- {両足|りょうあし}で{立|た}つ: to stand on both feet
- {両足|りょうあし}を{広|ひろ}げる: to spread one's legs
- {両足|りょうあし}{骨折|こっせつ}: fractures in both legs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {片足|かたあし}: one foot/leg — paired opposite
- {両手|りょうて}: both hands — same pattern with hands
- {両腕|りょううで}: both arms
- {両肩|りょうかた}: both shoulders
